events.description: WVON radio station launched by Leonard and Phil Chess; becomes 'the voice during the civil rights movement.'
events.name: WVON launch

events.description: Carl Hansberry's 6140 S. Rhodes purchase breaks the Woodlawn Property Owners Association's 1928 covenant; case feeds NAACP momentum toward Shelley v. Kraemer (1948).
events.name: Hansberry v. Lee

events.description: NAACP victory outlawing enforcement of racially restrictive covenants; foreshadowed by Hansberry.
events.name: Shelley v. Kraemer

events.description: July 29, July 31, and August 5 open-housing marches centered on 63rd Street (Halverson Realty at 63rd & Kedzie; King's rock-struck march to a 63rd Street real-estate office).
events.name: 1966 open-housing marches on 63rd Street

events.description: TWO, led by spokesman/president Rev. Arthur M. Brazier, defeats the University of Chicago's Woodlawn expansion.
events.name: TWO defeats U of C Woodlawn expansion

events.description: Mayor Richard J. Daley dedicates the Englewood Shopping Center pedestrian mall at 63rd & Halsted; project later judged to have failed.
events.name: Englewood pedestrian mall dedication

events.description: El structure east of Cottage Grove demolished with <24 hours' public notice, over Woodlawn community opposition led by Rev. Arthur Brazier.
events.name: 1997 Jackson Park el demolition

events.description: Ahmad Jamal records landmark album 'But Not for Me' at the Pershing (Budland) on/near 63rd Street.
events.name: Ahmad Jamal Pershing recordings

events.description: White City Amusement Park (63rd & South Park) opens May 26, 1905; closes 1934 (rink to 1958).
events.name: White City opens

events.description: Kennedy-King College's 40-acre campus at 63rd & Halsted dedicated (~$192M).
events.name: Kennedy-King campus dedication

events.description: Sears anchor at 63rd & Halsted closes; Tribune documented split merchant reactions the same week.
events.name: Sears Englewood closes

organizations.description: Operated the Tivoli Theatre as an R&B/jazz showcase after its movie-palace years.
organizations.name: Balaban & Katz

organizations.description: Spearheaded the Englewood pedestrian-mall effort (per chicago-l.org).
organizations.name: Englewood Business Men's Association

organizations.description: Neighborhood organization led by Rev. Arthur M. Brazier; defeated U of C's 1963 Woodlawn expansion; later headquartered in the Washington Park National Bank building.
organizations.name: The Woodlawn Organization

organizations.description: Launched WVON April 1, 1963; station served as 'the voice during the civil rights movement.'
organizations.name: WVON

organizations.description: City college campus at 63rd & Halsted, dedicated July 18, 2007, on the former Englewood Mall site.
organizations.name: Kennedy-King College

organizations.description: Pastorate of Rev. Arthur M. Brazier (1960-2008) at 6320 S. Dorchester; corridor civic anchor.
organizations.name: Apostolic Church of God

organizations.description: Institution whose bank buildings anchor the corridor's finance function (815 W. 63rd, 1930; 6300 S. Cottage Grove, 1924).
organizations.name: Chicago City Bank and Trust Co. / Washington Park National Bank

people.description: Black owner of McKie's Disc Jockey Show Lounge (6323 S. Cottage Grove, 1955-66); later a WVON 'Good Guy' on-air personality. Corridor's documented club-to-radio link.
people.name: McKie Fitzhugh

people.description: Pastor of Apostolic Church of God (1960-2008); spokesman/president of TWO; led 1963 U of C expansion defeat and 1994 fight against el demolition.
people.name: Rev. Arthur M. Brazier

people.description: Purchased at 6140 S. Rhodes; Hansberry v. Lee (1940) broke the Woodlawn covenant.
people.name: Carl Hansberry

people.description: Landmark 1958 'But Not for Me' recordings at the Pershing (Budland) on the corridor; played the Kitty Kat Club (611 E. 63rd).
people.name: Ahmad Jamal

people.description: WVON 'Good Guy' personality; February 26, 1965 aircheck survives; narrated the 1969 KOCO documentary.
people.name: Herb Kent

people.description: Rock-struck on the August 5, 1966 open-housing march toward a 63rd Street real-estate office; interviewed on WVON.
people.name: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

people.description: Owners of Chess Records; bought WHFC-1450 AM and launched WVON April 1, 1963.
people.name: Leonard and Phil Chess

places.description: Regional shopping district; pedestrian mall (1969); Kennedy-King campus (2007); Englewood Square (2016).
places.name: 63rd Street & Halsted (Englewood)

places.description: Black commercial strip; Tivoli Theatre; Washington Park National Bank building; Green Line Cottage Grove terminal.
places.name: 63rd Street & Cottage Grove (Woodlawn)

places.description: Jackson Park elevated branch built directly over 63rd Street; structure east of Cottage Grove demolished 1997.
places.name: Elevated line over 63rd Street

places.description: Hotel complex: Pershing Lounge/Budland (Jamal 1958 recordings) and Pershing Ballroom (Charlie Parker 1950).
places.name: Pershing Hotel complex

places.description: Amusement park 1905-1934 (rink to 1958); ballroom, tower; de facto segregated in early years.
places.name: White City Amusement Park (63rd & South Park)

places.description: 6201 S. Cottage Grove; opened Dec 6, 1922; demolished 1967.
places.name: Trianon Ballroom

places.description: 63rd & Cottage Grove; opened Feb 16, 1921; 3,520 seats; Balaban & Katz palace turned R&B/jazz showcase; closed 1963.
places.name: Tivoli Theatre

places.description: 815 W. 63rd; completed 1930; architect Abraham Epstein; Art Deco; cornerstone 1929.
places.name: Chicago City Bank and Trust Co. Building

places.description: 6300 S. Cottage Grove; completed 1924; Cook County Land Bank acquisition 2018; redevelopment approved 2023.
places.name: Washington Park National Bank Building

places.description: 6323 S. Cottage Grove; 1955-66; Black-owned by McKie Fitzhugh; Coltrane, Muddy Waters played.
places.name: McKie's Disc Jockey Show Lounge

places.description: Halverson Realty at 63rd & Kedzie; site of July 1966 open-housing marches.
places.name: 63rd Street & Kedzie (march site)

places.description: Two Green Line terminals serving the corridor: Ashland/63rd and Cottage Grove.
places.name: Ashland/63rd and Cottage Grove terminals
